newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank chief sees low inflation in '97.
newsitem.headline: China central bank chief sees low inflation in '97.

text.p: China's inflation is expected to be low in 1997, enabling the central bank to focus on reform of monetary controls and reduction of unhealthy assets, People's Bank of China Governor Dai Xianglong said.

Dai forecast inflation at below a target of 6.0 percent in 1997, compared with a rise of 6.5 percent in the benchmark retail price index last year, the China Securities on Wednesday quoted Dai as saying.

"There will be no sudden rebound in inflation in 1997," the newspaper quoted Dai as saying, adding that the level this year would be low. Retail price inflation was up a year-on-year 2.9 percent in February.

The low level of inflation would enable the central bank to focus on reform and improvement of its financial controls, to reduce unhealthy assets and improve risk management, Dai said in a speech given in the southern town of Shenzhen.
He revealed that the bank would hold a national-level meeting in April to discuss detailed measures.
One issue to be discussed would be methods to guide securities houses to expand their scope of business into investment banking, Dai said.
